newsitem.title: JAPAN: DDI Corp shares weaker on downgrading.
newsitem.headline: DDI Corp shares weaker on downgrading.

text.p: Shares in DDI Corp declined after being ask-only in Tuesday morning trade, discouraged by a major foreign securities house's downgrading of the issue.
The provider of long-distance telephone services had fallen 49,000 yen to 790,000 by 0121 GMT. Trade volume was 2,158 shares.

Goldman Sachs said on Tuesday that it had cut its rating for DDI to "outperformer" from the "recommended list" because DDI's share price has outperformed the market by 20 percent over the past 12 months.
Analyst Eric Gan said DDI's group net profit would continue to recover gradually over the next few years.
But he added the cancellation rate of its PHS phones could rise to 55 percent in the year to end-March 1998, which would have a "large negative impact" on the PHS division's gross margin.
The PHS, or personal handyphone system, uses technology halfway between cellular and cordless phones. It costs less than full-powered cell phones and has more range than a regular cordless phone.
Gan said DDI would not be able to achieve its target of breaking even in its PHS division in fiscal 1997/98.
